title: Get Started in Adobe After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Create a composition and get comfortable with the workspace.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Make a five-second composition. Add a solid, rename it, and save your project.

title: Import and Organize Files in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Import media without turning your project into a pile of missing files.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Create folders for footage, audio, and compositions. Import one image and rename it.

title: Setting Keyframes to Create Animations in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Understand keyframes, timing, and spacing.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Animate a square from left to right. Move the second keyframe closer and compare the speed.

title: Animating Text in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Create, style, and animate a text layer.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Animate your name into frame. Make a second version with a different entrance.

title: Animate Shape Layers in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Work with fills, strokes, paths, and shape transforms.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Draw a simple line icon and animate its stroke appearing. Use only native shape tools.

title: Adjust Anchor Points in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Understand why a layer rotates or scales from the wrong place.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Rotate a rectangle around its center, then around its bottom edge. Compare the results.

title: Effects in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Native effects and adjustment layers after core animation.
caveat: Useful reference; avoid prioritizing effects before timing.

title: Create & Animate Masks in After Effects - AE Fundamantals
reason: Create and animate masks to control a layer’s visibility.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Reveal a word with an animated rectangular mask. Try changing the feather.

title: Create & Animate Mattes in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Use alpha and luma mattes, including the newer matte controls.
caveat: Uses the track matte controls introduced in After Effects 2023.
practice: Reveal a title with a separate shape layer, then animate the title independently.

title: Parent Layers & Properties in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Use parenting and nulls to control a group of layers.
caveat: Video interfaces may look different from your version of After Effects.
practice: Parent a title and two shapes to one null. Move the group while retaining their own animation.

title: How to Render Video Files in After Effects - AE Fundamentals
reason: Understand the render queue, formats, and transparency.
caveat: Direct H.264 export shown is for After Effects 2023 or newer. Older versions use Media Encoder.
practice: Export your five-second animation as an MP4 and play it outside After Effects.

title: 2022 After Effects Jumpstart | Beginner tutorial
reason: A 7-minute first composition and title project.
caveat: AE 2022 interface; older export workflow.

title: Graph Editor for Beginners – After Effects Tutorial That Actually Makes Sense
reason: Compare the speed and value graphs and shape your easing.
caveat: Includes an AEJuice sponsor segment. Focus on the built-in Graph Editor lesson.
practice: Make three versions of the same move: linear, Easy Ease, and a custom curve.

title: The LAST graph editor tutorial you'll ever need. \\ After Effects Tutorial
reason: Timing and spacing plus separate speed/value graph chapters.
caveat: Longer than the core lesson; sponsor segment and course promotion.

title: The GAME CHANGING New Track Matte System in After Effects 2023
reason: Explains the change to the AE 2023 matte system.
caveat: Use when learners are confused by older track-matte tutorials.

title: Parenting & Null Objects Explained in After Effects
reason: Short parenting/null overview with a tracking application.
caveat: Preview pacing and tracking prerequisites before expanding its role.

title: How to Use Parenting and Null Objects | After Effects Tutorial for Motion Graphics | Adobe Video
reason: Adobe-hosted explanation of parenting and nulls by Kyle Hamrick.
caveat: Use as a second explanation, not a new skill requirement.

title: Complete Intro to Motion Design | FULL AFTER EFFECTS COURSE
reason: Follow a longer motion-design project with text, shapes, and animation.
caveat: A longer follow-up project, not a first-day introduction. Set aside several practice sessions.
practice: Work through one chapter at a time. Then change the type, colors, and timing to make your own version.

title: After Effects: Building a Simple Clean Intro & Transition
reason: A compact intro/transition project with modest discovery.
caveat: 2018 interface; description promotes Dojo Shifter. Verify whether the demonstrated workflow needs the tool.

title: Shape Layers in After Effects – Complete Beginner Guide
reason: Chapters cover shape hierarchy, trims, strokes, groups, and modifiers.
caveat: Dense 29-minute reference; review teaching and pacing before recommending to first-day learners.

title: How to Use Shape Layers in After Effects | Trim Paths, Repeater & More
reason: Very short shape-layer overview.
caveat: The description promises many topics in 2:34; brevity and low views are not evidence of teaching quality.
